transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just can't make myself go near the front windows at work anymore. Or even that part of the street, honestly. I work in retail, and I keep finding excuses to stay in the back room, even though being out front is a big part of my job. I just... I can't do it right now, and it's becoming a real problem.
Is there something specific that you're afraid of when you think about being near the front windows at work?

Well, yeah. A little while ago, a car crashed right through the front of the store while I was working. Now, the crash just keeps popping into my head out of nowhere. It's really bad when I'm trying to set up displays near the front. Suddenly, it's like... I can hear the loud bang all over again, and I can actually see the glass coming down. It just feels like it's happening right in front of me again.
Are there any other situations or places that you're avoiding because of the car crash?

Um, no, not really. I haven't noticed myself avoiding anything else. It's... it's mostly just the store. Like, I still drive my own car fine, and going to other places hasn't been an issue. It really just seems to be that specific spot at work where it actually happened.
Do you ever have the memory of the car crash popping into your head when you're not near the store or thinking about work?

Um, no, not really. I don't think so. It's pretty much just tied to the store. When I'm at home or out doing other things, it doesn't really pop into my head. It's just... mostly when I'm actually there, or maybe if I'm dreading going into my shift. But otherwise, no, I haven't noticed it happening.
How long have you been experiencing these memories and fears about the car crash at work?

It's been about two weeks now. Basically ever since it happened... it was during my overnight shift when the car actually crashed through the window. So, yeah, it's been going on for the last two weeks.
Have you been having trouble sleeping since the car crash happened?
No, my sleep has been fine, honestly. I haven't really had any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. It's just... normal.
Have you been startled more easily since the car crash happened?

Yeah, definitely. Um, if a delivery cart bangs in the back, or a car honks outside... or even if someone just comes up behind me, I jump really hard. Like, my whole body just jerks. And then my heart just keeps racing for a while afterward.
Have you been avoiding talking or thinking about the car crash?

No, not really. Um, I don't try to avoid it or anything. People at work ask me about it sometimes, and I'll talk to them about what happened. And I definitely still think about it... so, no, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding it.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I still like doing the same things I usually do. Like, I still enjoy hanging out with my friends and watching my regular shows. So, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in anything.
Has your difficulty with being near the front windows at work caused any problems in your relationships with coworkers or supervisors?

Yeah, it kind of has. Um, the other day I actually had to leave right in the middle of a window reset because I just couldn't finish the work. I had to walk away from it. And honestly... now I'm just really worried that I can't handle the parts of my job that involve the storefront at all. So it's definitely causing some stress at work.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're not in a situation that would normally be considered dangerous?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not really looking over my shoulder everywhere I go or anything. Besides the thing with the windows at work, I feel pretty normal when I'm just out and about. So, no, I haven't noticed myself being extra on edge or looking out for threats like that.
Have you noticed any difficulties in your personal relationships or daily life outside of work due to your feelings or reactions to the car crash?

No, not really. Um, my life outside of work is pretty much exactly the same as it was. I'm still seeing my friends and doing my normal stuff at home, and nobody's said I'm acting differently or anything. It's really just that specific thing at the store that's been a problem for me. So, no, my relationships and everything else are fine.
Do you feel guilty about what happened with the car crash at work?

No, I don't feel guilty. Um, I mean, I was just inside working when it happened. I didn't have anything to do with the car actually crashing into the building, you know? It was the driver's fault. So... no, I don't have any guilt about it. It was just a really scary thing that happened.
Have you been feeling anxious or distressed even when you're not thinking about the car crash or near the front windows at work?

No, not really. Um, like I said, outside of work, I feel pretty normal. I'm not just sitting around feeling anxious or upset for no reason. It's really only when I'm near those windows at the store that I get that panicked feeling. Otherwise, I'm okay.
Have you been avoiding other things or activities at work besides being near the front windows?

No, it's really just the windows. Um, I still do everything else I'm supposed to do. I'll work the registers if they're further back, or go to the stockroom, or do inventory... it's literally just that one spot at the front of the store. As long as I'm away from the glass, I can do the rest of my job fine.
Have you been avoiding the store altogether on your days off or when you're not working?

No, not really. I mean, I don't usually go in on my days off anyway, just because it's work, you know? But if I had to run in to buy something or talk to my manager, I'd still go inside. I would just... I'd just make sure to stay away from the front area. So, no, I'm not avoiding the whole building.
Have you ever had a day where you didn't think about the car crash at all?

No, I don't think so. It... it just keeps popping into my head out of nowhere. Like, I'll be trying to set up displays or something, and suddenly I can just hear that loud bang again. And... and I see the glass coming down, just like it's happening right then. So, no, I haven't really had a day where it hasn't crossed my mind.
Do you feel a strong physical reaction, like your heart racing or sweating, when you think about the car crash or see something that reminds you of it?

No, not really. I mean, I don't get sweaty or feel like my heart is beating out of my chest or anything. It's more just... it's just in my head, you know? Like I said, the memories just pop up and I hear the sound, but my body doesn't really react like that. I just feel a little tense, maybe, but no racing heart or anything like you're asking.
